document.intro: A real kiosk with its signs. The names on the signs are newspapers: the kiosk tells you what the town reads, and it also takes parcels. Read the signs before you read the paper.
document.fact: Many German kiosks also handle parcels: they are pick-up points for the post, with a yellow sign, and a queue of everyone who wasn’t home when the delivery came.
document.tasks[2].instruction: Join the sentences with dessen or deren.
reading.title: Leserbriefe
reading.intro: Lena’s cousin Vroni has been given the letters page of the local paper to run. Herr Doktor Brummer, a retired teacher whose letters have been arriving twice a week since 1987, has a complaint. He has come to the newsroom in person. Vroni’s intern, a very young man called Timo, opens the door.
reading.fact: Germany still has a great many daily newspapers, most of them local. The letters page is read with attention: a *Leserbrief* is a respected form, and an annoyed one is a sport.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Complete with the right form of the noun.
